answer: A tight ring of 72 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Because the jetty calculation reruns each epoch, the vertex weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the pulse settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 42% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 2 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
